analysis.one_liner: DMart (Avenue Supermarts) runs a chain of value-format supermarkets and hypermarkets selling groceries, FMCG, general merchandise and apparel, mostly out of stores it owns rather than leases.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (announced ~Oct 10-12, 2026) showed revenue up ~18% YoY to about ₹19,644 cr, but PAT grew only 8.5% to ₹743 cr as EBITDA margin slipped to 7.1% from 7.3% a year earlier on rising entry-level wage costs. The stock fell to a fresh 52-week low of ₹3,342, down ~12% in October alone, and Citi reiterated a 'sell' view saying profitability continues to lag revenue growth.
analysis.plain_terms: DMart keeps growing sales at a healthy mid-to-high-teens pace and keeps opening stores (518 now, 15 added this quarter), but each extra rupee of revenue is now converting into less profit than before because staff costs are rising faster than DMart can offset in a low-margin value-retail format. The stock is down 38% from its September 2024 peak with no split or demerger behind that fall - it's a straightforward derating, not a chart artifact. The open question is whether this is a temporary cost bump or a sign that DMart's famously efficient model is losing some edge to wage inflation and quick-commerce competition.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): revenue ₹19,644 cr (+18% YoY), PAT ₹743 cr (+8.5% YoY). EBITDA margin fell to 7.1% from 7.3%, PAT margin to 3.8% from 4.1%, as employee costs rose ~20% YoY (management cited entry-level wage inflation). On the positive side, same-store sales growth for stores 2+ years old improved to 9.5% from 6.8% a year ago - a genuine volume gain even as margins slipped. General merchandise & apparel (the higher-margin categories) held roughly flat at ~23.6% of H1 revenue versus 23.3% prior year. Preceding quarters: Q1 FY27 ₹18,795 cr/₹860 cr; Q4 FY26 ₹17,684 cr/₹656 cr; Q3 FY26 ₹18,101 cr/₹856 cr; Q2 FY26 ₹16,676 cr/₹685 cr - profit growth has repeatedly undershot revenue growth across these quarters, not just this one.
analysis.performance_read: No split or demerger complicates this stock's price history, so the fall can be read at face value as a real derating, not a chart artifact. The stock sits at its 52-week low of ₹3,342, 38% below its September 2024 peak of ₹5,391. Over 1 year it is down 22.6% versus a 9.5% fall in the Nifty and a 38% fall in peer Trent, so both value-retail names have had a rough year. The longer picture is worse for DMart specifically: over 3 and 5 years it is down 13% and 32% respectively while the Nifty is up 17% and 25%, and Trent is up 43% and 157%. This has been a multi-year underperformer against both the market and its closest listed peer.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 70x trailing earnings and ~8.3x book, DMart remains priced well above the broader market and above estimates of the general retail-sector median P/E (cited near 24x by one source), even after this fall. The 'why it got cheaper' part is clear: profit growth has lagged revenue growth for several quarters, eroding the premium investors paid for DMart's execution track record. Whether the current ~70x multiple is itself cheap is a separate question - it still prices in a long runway of growth and margin recovery that hasn't shown up in the numbers yet.
analysis.growth_read: Currently volume-led, not margin-led. Revenue is growing at high-teens rates, same-store sales growth is accelerating (9.5% vs 6.8% a year ago), and store count keeps rising (518, +15 this quarter) - real volume growth. But margins are moving the wrong way, with EBITDA margin down to 7.1% from 7.3% and PAT margin to 3.8% from 4.1% on wage inflation. Rising volume with falling margin is a weaker combination for a thin-margin retailer than the 'both growing' story that underwrote DMart's historically high multiples.
analysis.health_read: This looks like a business/competitive-margin question, not a financial-risk one. DMart pays no dividend and reinvests fully into store expansion; borrowings have risen from ₹592 cr (Mar 2024) to ₹2,425 cr (Mar 2026), but that's still small against a ₹29,518 cr asset base and consistent with capex for new owned stores rather than distress. ROCE of ~17-19% and ROE of ~13% show capital is still being deployed productively, just less productively than before. The real risk to watch is competitive/margin pressure (wage costs, quick-commerce and online grocery competition), not leverage.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters - the Damani family (Radhakishan Damani ~23%, Gopikishan Damani ~5.6%, Bright Star Investments ~13.6%, and others) - hold about 74.5%, unchanged, with 0% pledged shares, a clean high-conviction holding. FIIs hold ~9.2%, DIIs ~8.7%, and public float is thin at ~6.4%. One minor promoter-group member (7,100 shares, following a family estate transmission) was reclassified to the public category in September 2026 - an immaterial, non-signalling event. Not verified: no other widely-tracked marquee outside investor appears on the register beyond the founder-promoter group itself.
strengths: Same-store sales growth for mature (2-year+) stores accelerated to 9.5% in Q2 FY27 from 6.8% a year earlier
Zero promoter pledging on a 74.5% holding, unusually clean among large-cap promoters
ROCE of ~17-19%, well above broader retail-sector medians despite the margin dip
Revenue growth of ~18% YoY with 15 new stores added this quarter (518 total) - expansion pace hasn't slowed
watchpoints: EBITDA margin down to 7.1% from 7.3% and PAT margin to 3.8% from 4.1% YoY, driven by ~20% YoY employee cost growth
Stock down 22.6% over 1 year and 38% from its September 2024 peak, now at a fresh 52-week low with no corporate action behind the move
P/E of ~70x and P/B of ~8.3x remain well above sector medians even after the recent derating
5-year return of -32% versus peer Trent's +157% - a multi-year gap, not a one-quarter blip
analysis.one_thing: Whether EBITDA margin stabilizes and recovers toward the ~7.6%+ levels of a couple of years ago over the next 1-2 quarters - that single number will show whether the wage-driven margin compression is temporary or a more structural shift in DMart's low-cost model.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue, PAT and margin figures were cross-checked across Business Standard, Zee Business, Multibagg and Screener.in and were consistent. P/E estimates varied across sources (70x on Screener vs. 73-81x cited elsewhere) - used Screener's ~70x as the more conservative, frequently-updated figure rather than averaging the spread. Could not independently verify the scale of any decline in DMart's online arm (DMart Ready) beyond passing headline mentions, so no figure is given for it. Debt, ROE, ROCE and shareholding percentages are from Screener.in and Trendlyne as of their most recent published data.
